mainTopic: How big is the 'large date' (כותבת הגסה) that makes one liable for eating on יום כיפור, and how this measure compares to a כביצה
overview: This amud continues רב פפא's question: is the large-date measure for יום כיפור counted with the pit or without it? רב אשי asks a similar question about a bone the size of a barley grain. He asks whether that grain is measured with its husk, and whether it is wet or dry. The גמרא explains that each אמורא found the other's question obvious. 'Large' means as big as possible, so the pit counts. The name 'barley' only fits a dry grain in its husk. Next, רב יהודה rules that the large date is a bit more than a כביצה, because that amount settles a person's mind. The גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא. In it, רבן גמליאל ate two dates in the סוכה only as a personal stringency, and רבי צדוק ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה. Together these suggest that two dates are under a כביצה, and the answer to this challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the date measure include the pit?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the 'date-bulk' for יום כיפור is measured with the pit or without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The date-bulk that the Sages spoke about: is it measured with its pit or without its pit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב פפא's question on the previous amud. He wants to know whether the date-sized amount of food that makes you liable on יום כיפור is measured with the date's pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה set the measure as a large date (כותבת הגסה). A date with its pit is bigger than one without it. So the answer changes how much food is needed for liability.

keyTerms.meaning: A date; the measure for eating on יום כיפור
Pit or seed of a fruit

phrases.english: The date-bulk that they said,
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's measure for eating on יום כיפור

phrases.english: with its pit, or without its pit?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּכוֹתֶבֶת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּגַרְעִינָתָהּ אוֹ בְּלֹא גַּרְעִינָתָהּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the date's pit counts toward the measure

steps.title: A parallel question about the barley-grain measure
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the barley-grain measure for a bone's טומאה is measured with or without the husk, and wet or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: a bone the size of a barley grain — is that with its husk or without its husk, a wet grain or a dry one?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a question similar to רב פפא's, but about a different measure. A bone the size of a barley grain makes things טמא, and he wants to know how to measure that grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like a date's pit, a barley grain's husk and its moisture change its size. רב אשי asks two things: whether the husk counts, and whether we use a fresh grain or a dried one.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone the size of a barley grain (a measure for טומאת מת)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
A bone the size of a barley grain,
with its husk or without its husk,
a wet grain or a dry one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question about a different measure
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the husk counts, and whether a wet or dry grain is used for the barley measure

steps.title: Why רב אשי did not ask רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: The word 'large' (גסה) tells רב אשי that the measure is as big as possible, which includes the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי had no question about רב פפא's case. Since the word 'large' was said, it means as large as possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב אשי did not wonder about the date's pit. To him the answer was obvious from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not just say 'a date'. It said 'a large date'. רב אשי reads that as 'make it as big as possible', so the pit is included.

keyTerms.meaning: He had no question about it (the answer was clear to him)
As large as it can be

phrases.english: Rav Ashi had no question
about this question of Rav Pappa,
since 'large' was stated —
it means as large as possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי לָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב פפא's question was obvious to רב אשי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'large' means the biggest size, so the pit is included

steps.title: Why רב פפא did not ask רב אשי's question
steps.stepSummary: A wet grain is called שיבולת and a shelled one is called אושלא, so 'barley' means a dry grain in its husk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא had no question about רב אשי's case. A wet grain is called 'שיבולת', and one without its husk is called 'אושלא'.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains the other side: why רב פפא did not wonder about the barley measure. To him the answer was clear from what people call the grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A grain only goes by the name 'barley' (שעורה) when it is dry and still in its husk. Once it is wet or shelled, it has a different name. So the משנה's word 'barley' must mean a dry grain with its husk.

keyTerms.meaning: Ear of grain (the name for fresh, wet barley)

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא thought the other's question was obvious. The date measure includes the pit ('large' means as big as possible). The barley measure is a dry grain in its husk (the name 'barley' only fits that).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa had no question
about this question of Rav Ashi:
a wet one is called 'shibbolet',
one without its husk is called 'ushla'.
phrases.notes: So 'barley' means dry and in its husk

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא לָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name 'barley' only applies to a dry grain in its husk

steps.title: The large date is more than an egg-bulk
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that כותבת הגסה is more than a כביצה, because that amount settles a person's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that רב יהודה said: the large date that the Sages spoke about is more than an egg-bulk. The Sages know that this amount settles a person's mind, and less than this does not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement gives an actual size for the date measure: a little more than an egg (כביצה). It also explains why that size was chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the מצוה is to afflict yourself (עינוי). Eating only breaks the affliction once you eat enough to feel settled (מיושב דעתו). The Sages had a tradition that this happens at slightly more than a כביצה.

keyTerms.meaning: More than the size of an egg
The Sages have an established tradition or knowledge
His mind is settled (he no longer feels afflicted)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical amount for liability on יום כיפור. It ties that amount to how a person feels, not to a random size.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Yehuda said:
the large date that they spoke of
is more than an egg-bulk.
And the Sages have it established
that with this amount his mind is settled;
with less than this, his mind is not settled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to measure a date to how big the date measure actually is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותבת הגסה is slightly more than a כביצה, the amount that settles the mind

steps.title: Challenge from the story of two dates and the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבן גמליאל ate two dates in the סוכה only as a personal stringency. That implies two dates are less than a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: there was an incident where they brought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי a cooked dish to taste, and they brought רבן גמליאל two dates and a bucket of water. They said: bring them up to the סוכה. And it was taught about this: not because that is the הלכה, but because they wanted to be strict on themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's measure with a ברייתא about food eaten on סוכות. The ברייתא says these Sages did not have to eat the two dates in the סוכה; they were only being strict on themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food of a כביצה or more must be eaten in the סוכה. If two dates did not require a סוכה, then two dates together must be less than a כביצה. In that case a single date is much smaller than a כביצה, which contradicts רב יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'two dates are less than a כביצה' outright. The גמרא infers it: the ברייתא says no סוכה was required, and only less than a כביצה is exempt.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וְהֵבִיאוּ לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: There was an incident: they brought to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
a cooked dish to taste,
and to Rabban Gamliel two dates
and a bucket of water.
And they said: bring them up to the sukkah.
And it was taught about this:
not because that is the halacha,
but because they wanted to be strict on themselves.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that one large date is more than a כביצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two dates did not require a סוכה, so they are less than a כביצה. One date must then be far less than a כביצה.

steps.title: רבי צדוק shows that less than an egg needs no סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי צדוק ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה, without washing and without ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they gave רבי צדוק food less than an egg-bulk, he took it with a cloth, ate it outside the סוכה, and did not make a blessing after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues with רבי צדוק's practice. It shows that food under a כביצה does not need a סוכה, washing, or ברכת המזון. This sets the background rule that makes the challenge work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי צדוק's actions show that the כביצה line is the cutoff for a real meal. That confirms the step-6 inference: if the two dates were exempt from the סוכה, they were under a כביצה. The challenge against רב יהודה now stands, waiting for an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth (used so he did not touch the food and need to wash hands)
He did not recite a blessing afterward (ברכת המזון)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key source for the rule that under a כביצה is a snack (אכילת עראי). Such food is exempt from the סוכה, from washing, and from ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
food less than an egg-bulk —
he took it with a cloth
phrases.notes: So he did not need to wash his hands

phrases.english: and ate it outside the sukkah,
and did not recite a blessing after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹכֶל פָּחוֹת מִכְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and sets out the כביצה cutoff behind the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's measure of more than a כביצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under a כביצה needs no סוכה. The two dates needed no סוכה, so two dates are under a כביצה, against רב יהודה.
